about: Thresholds for the survey insights. scripts/survey_insights.py reads this file and its CLI defaults come from it. Counts are survey respondents (customers) or survey events in the window the user chose. Shares are fractions (0.25 means 25%). Each key is explained under notes.

notes.confidence: Confidence level of every interval the script prints (response rates, answer shares, NPS and CSAT).
notes.min_responses: A survey with fewer respondents than this in the window, or a score with fewer answers than this, is too few to trust: the score is shown but labelled, and the survey is flagged high priority.
notes.small_sample: A score with at least min_responses but fewer than this many answers gets a confidence note (the interval is wide). At or above it, no note.
notes.nps_star_counts: A rating-stars question with this many stars is read as an NPS-style question (promoters minus detractors). With 10 stars the scale is 1 to 10, not 0 to 10, and the output says so.
notes.nps_promoter_min: Answers at or above this score are promoters on an NPS-style question.
notes.nps_passive_min: Answers at or above this score (and below nps_promoter_min) are passives; anything lower is a detractor.
notes.csat_top_box: For a rating-stars question with this many stars (the key), how many top scores count as satisfied (the value). 5 stars with 2 means 4 and 5 are satisfied. Star counts not listed here and not in nps_star_counts get an average score only.
notes.skip_flag_share: A question answered by fewer than this share of the survey's respondents is one everybody skips (medium priority; high when it is mandatory, which points at tracking).
notes.low_response_rate: When respondents divided by customers shown or sent the survey is below this, the response rate is low (medium priority). Only checked when the user gives a shown or sent count.
notes.other_flag_share: When typed-in Other answers make up at least this share of a choice question's answers, the choices are missing something people want to say (low priority). Their text is never listed.
notes.stale_edit_days: An active survey not edited for at least this many days is flagged for review (low priority); an active survey with no responses in the window is flagged high whatever its age.
notes.trend_min_weekly: Weekly response trends are only judged when the median of the earlier full weeks is at least this many responses, so tiny surveys don't flag noise.
notes.trend_drop_share: When the latest full week's responses are below this share of the median of the earlier full weeks, responses dropped (medium priority): check the survey link, the campaign that carries it and tracking.
notes.min_split_group: In a split (by device, country or another non-personal property), groups with fewer answers than this are shown but marked too small to compare.
notes.max_answer_values: The grouping top N to use for answer distributions, and the most answer values the script lists per question. Rarer values are added up as the rest.
notes.free_text_sample_cap: The largest grouping top N the assistant may use when the user explicitly asks for themes in free-text answers. The script never prints free-text values; it only counts them.
